raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

JointThreshold decoding already has a batched tensor implementation, but CUDA defaults to the per-row Python path. At higher concurrency, that path serializes argmax, confidence, edit, and completion work across requests and repeatedly synchronizes the host with the device.

This PR enables the existing vectorized JointThreshold path by default on CUDA. The change targets JointThreshold specifically: LowConfidence is already vectorized, and DiffusionGemma uses the separate Gemma4Renoise sampler.

## Modifications

- Default `vectorized_decoding` to true on CUDA, matching the existing NPU policy.
- Preserve `vectorized_decoding: false` as a compatibility/debug escape hatch.
- Document the default and its applicability to `LLaDA2MoeModelLM`, `SDARForCausalLM`, and `SDARMoeForCausalLM`.

## Accuracy Tests

SGLang already has a registered CUDA E2E test for this exact path:
`test/registered/dllm/test_dllm_fdfo_joint_threshold.py`. It launches
`inclusionAI/LLaDA2.1-mini` with JointThreshold and requires byte-identical
outputs between FDFO and synchronous execution. Since this PR changes the CUDA
default, both arms exercise the vectorized implementation.

I also ran an external real-model E2E A/B matrix by launching two SGLang HTTP
servers with `sglang.launch_server` and driving them with
`sglang.benchmark.serving`. All 3,968/3,968 measured LLaDA2.1-mini requests
completed with the requested output token count and no request errors.

This validates the real serving path and output completion, not downstream task
accuracy. No locally available SDAR checkpoint was available, so this PR does
not claim real-model SDAR coverage.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Configuration:

- H200, TP1, BF16, FDFO;
- FlashInfer attention;
- radix cache disabled;
- maximum 128 running requests;
- 8,192-token context;
- exact token-ID inputs;
- baseline and vectorized arms used identical server and benchmark settings;
- each result below contains 32, 64, 128, 256, or 512 requests at concurrency 1, 8, 32, 64, or 128 respectively.

**Metric definitions:** request throughput is the achieved end-to-end client
throughput (`completed requests / benchmark duration`). TPOT is time per output
token excluding the first token:
`(request E2E latency - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1)`. The latency columns below
are TPOT, not full end-to-end request latency.

### Decode-heavy: 512 input / 2,048 output tokens

| Concurrency | E2E request throughput | Delta | Mean TPOT | Delta | p95 TPOT | Delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.172 -> 0.168 req/s | -2.7% | 2.72 -> 2.79 ms | +2.8% | 5.07 -> 5.20 ms | +2.5% |
| 8 | 0.532 -> 0.685 req/s | +28.7% | 6.89 -> 5.03 ms | -27.0% | 12.87 -> 10.66 ms | -17.2% |
| 32 | 0.774 -> 1.079 req/s | +39.4% | 17.60 -> 12.40 ms | -29.6% | 31.66 -> 22.11 ms | -30.2% |
| 64 | 1.001 -> 1.493 req/s | +49.2% | 27.67 -> 18.32 ms | -33.8% | 54.96 -> 37.30 ms | -32.1% |
| 128 | 1.158 -> 1.842 req/s | +59.0% | 48.08 -> 29.78 ms | -38.1% | 100.22 -> 64.81 ms | -35.3% |

### Long-prefill: 4,096 input / 1,536 output tokens

| Concurrency | E2E request throughput | Delta | Mean TPOT | Delta | p95 TPOT | Delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.269 -> 0.258 req/s | -4.0% | 1.84 -> 1.91 ms | +3.7% | 5.06 -> 5.20 ms | +2.8% |
| 8 | 0.641 -> 0.674 req/s | +5.2% | 6.61 -> 6.44 ms | -2.6% | 25.42 -> 24.67 ms | -3.0% |
| 32 | 0.878 -> 0.924 req/s | +5.2% | 20.29 -> 19.36 ms | -4.6% | 70.97 -> 62.97 ms | -11.3% |
| 64 | 0.984 -> 1.119 req/s | +13.8% | 36.76 -> 32.41 ms | -11.9% | 138.68 -> 122.23 ms | -11.9% |
| 128 | 1.173 -> 1.308 req/s | +11.5% | 61.80 -> 56.39 ms | -8.8% | 237.48 -> 219.20 ms | -7.7% |

A GPU-swapped control reproduced the concurrency-64 gains:

- decode-heavy: +49.0% request throughput and -33.4% mean TPOT;
- long-prefill: +12.5% request throughput and -10.2% mean TPOT.

The batch-1 regression is an intentional tradeoff for one consistent CUDA execution path; the benefit grows with batch size because it removes per-request Python work and host synchronization.

Benchmark runtime used PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130` and FlashInfer `0.6.14`. Current SGLang pins FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the pre-commit configuration.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -63,8 +63,17 @@ max_post_edit_steps: 16
 # 2-gram repetition penalty (default 0).
 # An empirical value of 3 is often sufficient to mitigate most repetitions.
 penalty_lambda: 0
+# CUDA and Ascend NPU use batched tensor operations for all batch sizes by
+# default. Set this to false only for compatibility or debugging.
+vectorized_decoding: true
 ```
 
+`JointThreshold` vectorization applies to the native mask-based dLLM
+architectures `LLaDA2MoeModelLM`, `SDARForCausalLM`, and
+`SDARMoeForCausalLM`. `LowConfidence` is already vectorized for these
+architectures. DiffusionGemma uses the separate `Gemma4Renoise` sampler, so
+this setting does not affect it.
+
 ## Example Client Code Snippet
 
 Just like other supported models, diffusion language models can be used via the REST API or Python client.

 from sglang.srt.dllm.config import DllmConfig
 from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardBatch
-from sglang.srt.utils import is_npu
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_cuda, is_npu
 
+_is_cuda = is_cuda()
 _is_npu = is_npu()
 
 
@@ -120,10 +121,12 @@ def __init__(self, config: DllmConfig):
             "max_post_edit_steps", 16
         )
         self.penalty_lambda = config.algorithm_config.get("penalty_lambda", 0)
-        # NPU defaults to the batched (vectorized) path; other platforms keep the
-        # upstream per-row path unless explicitly overridden via algorithm_config.
+        # CUDA and NPU use the batched path for every batch size. This removes
+        # per-request host synchronizations and keeps one execution path across
+        # synchronous and FDFO decoding. Other platforms retain the per-row
+        # default until they are benchmarked.
         self.vectorized_decoding = config.algorithm_config.get(
-            "vectorized_decoding", _is_npu
+            "vectorized_decoding", _is_cuda or _is_npu
         )
         # The sync loop advances one shared batched state in place across steps;
         # FDFO must carry state per request, so it gathers/scatters each round.
